title: Give launch OSD a finite duration so a lost close can't leave it up

leads.summary: The 13-second backstop outlives the retained launch deadline when #12966 also merges
leads.consequence: #12966 starts launchTimeout only if it is stopped, while restarting launchDelay on every launch. The two PRs merge without a textual conflict and their current tests pass. On a repeat launch at t=12s, the second OSD show is sent at t=14s with duration=13s, but the preserved timeout is due at t=15s. If close IPC is lost, the fallback now lasts until t=27s instead of the intended original t=15s. A later arrival of show also shifts expiration. #13095 has the same retained-deadline behavior for repeat launches of the same app; its duration hunk conflicts, and manually choosing this PR's constant would retain the mismatch. Compute duration from the actual remaining deadline (clamped), or reconcile the retrigger policies before combining. This is a cross-PR defect, not a failure of #13536 alone at its pinned head.

leads.summary: Multiple open fixes change the same OSD show, and #13606 changes its timeout independently
leads.consequence: #13669 and #11568 instead use 15000ms and conflict at both the comment and show call; #13095 selects launchTimeout.interval for duration and conflicts at show; #13606 selects a 5000ms show plus an 8000ms timeout and conflicts at show; #9819 replaces detached IPC with in-process summon and conflicts at show. These are alternatives, not stacked PRs. A maintainer must choose and coordinate one policy; resolving #13606's show conflict by retaining this PR's 13000ms while accepting its 8000ms timeout would leave a lost-close launch OSD visible until t=15s rather than its intended t=8s. GitHub's mergeable state of the other PRs against quattro is not a prediction of merging them together. This is an integration warning, not a defect of the pinned head in isolation.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** No defects found; several open PRs change the same `osd show` line in different ways (see Related open PRs).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (source, plus a timer model that runs the real `AppLibrary.qml`, `Osd.qml` and `OsdModel.js` function bodies with stand-in timers and IPC):
- The payload's `duration` is 15000 - 2000 = 13000 ms, which the OSD's `hideTimer` uses as its interval. At this head both launch timers always restart together, so 13 s is exactly the time left on `launchTimeout`.
- Close lost, close arriving before the show, and a windowless app whose timeout close is lost: `quattro` leaves "Launching X…" up until something else closes or replaces it; this head hides it about 15 s after the click.
- Fast and slow launches, a relaunch at 10 s, and a volume OSD shown during or after a launch behave as on `quattro`. Every OSD goes through `show()`, which restarts or stops `hideTimer`, so the launch card's timer cannot dismiss another OSD.
- `test/shell.d/app-search-test.sh` and `osd-test.sh` pass at this head.

**Residual (by design):** the change bounds the show/close race rather than removing it. If the window maps right at the 2 s mark and the close overtakes the show, the card still stays about 13 s after the app opened. Open issue #8242 covers the same race and the choice between a cap and in-process calls.

**One normal-path difference:** a relaunch just before 15 s leaves a gap of up to about 2 s with no card, where `quattro` kept the first card up.
</details>

<details><summary>Related open PRs</summary>

- #11568, #13669, #13095: the same cap with 15000 ms (a stranded card lasts until about 17 s). All conflict with this PR on the `osd show` line. #13669 also says it fixes #13535.
- #13606: 5 s duration, 8 s timeout and a window poll; conflicts on the same line.
- #9819, #12115: send show and close in-process, which removes the race; both conflict.
- #12966 merges cleanly, but then a relaunch keeps the first launch's deadline while its card still gets 13 s from its own show. Modelled: relaunch at 12 s, card shown at 14.04 s, `launchTimeout` fires at 15 s, and with that close lost the card stays until 27.04 s. #13095 does the same for a same-app relaunch if the conflicting line is resolved to this PR's expression. The card stays bounded, but the comment's "the rest of launchTimeout" would no longer hold.
</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

- **Optional test improvement:** no test covers the new duration. This assertion, added after the existing launch-feedback check in `test/shell.d/app-search-test.sh`, fails on the merge-base and passes at this head (it pins source text, like the file's other AppLibrary checks):

```js
const launchDelayMatch = appLibraryQml.match(/id: launchDelay[\s\S]*?\n  \}/)
assert(launchDelayMatch, 'app library launchDelay timer exists')
assert(
  launchDelayMatch[0].includes('duration: launchTimeout.interval - launchDelay.interval'),
  'launch OSD expires on its own when launchTimeout would have closed it'
)
```

Actual output at the merge-base (exit 1): `not ok - launch OSD expires on its own when launchTimeout would have closed it`. At this head (exit 0): `ok - launch OSD expires on its own when launchTimeout would have closed it`.
- The updated comment could also say the duration covers a close that lands before the show, which the PR description names.
- #13535 describes the same problem as the open #8242; referencing it would link the two.
</details>
